title: Spider-Man After Civil War
subtitle: Back in Black to now
blurb: The end of the classic run, then eighteen years of recommendations — 378 issues, tracked one by one.
notes: Start with the Civil War list.
Back in Black reads directly on from the last issue of Civil War. Before that, the whole run from 1962 is in Amazing Spider-Man.

1 is Back in Black and One More Day, finishing the story the earlier lists were telling. 2 is Superior Spider-Man, the one run every guide singles out. 3 is the rest — recommendations, not a list to complete, and outside the finish date.
Brand New Day and Big Time are selective.
Those two sections list the arcs worth reading rather than every issue of a hundred-issue stretch, which is how the source frames them. Every other section is complete.

The notes say what an entry is, never what happens in it. The eighteen years covered here are the most contested period in the character's history and the arguments are easy to find; none of them are here.
Selections from the checklist written for the group; the annotations are rewritten from it rather than copied, because that document spoils freely.

sections.title: Back in Black
sections.intro: Reads directly on from the last Civil War issue. If you have not read that list, start there — this arc is a reaction to it from the first page.

sections.title: One More Day
sections.sub: 2007 · four issues, in exactly this order
sections.intro: The most argued-about editorial decision in the character's history, and the line the classic run ends on. Best read in one sitting — and plenty of readers stop here on purpose.

sections.title: Brand New Day
sections.sub: 2008–10 · the arcs worth reading, issue by issue
sections.intro: From here on this is a set of recommendations rather than a list to finish, so these are the arcs the source picks out of a hundred-issue stretch — not every issue of it. Three issues a month, rotating writers, Peter single and broke and back in Queens. Better than its reputation.

items.note: “Brand New Day” begins — Slott and McNiven, and the banner runs to #564
The last issue to carry the Brand New Day banner
“New Ways to Die” begins — Slott and John Romita Jr.
“The Gauntlet” begins — a systematic reintroduction of the rogues
“Shed” begins — Zeb Wells and Chris Bachalo on the Lizard
“Grim Hunt” begins — the sequel to Kraven's Last Hunt, 23 years on

sections.title: Dan Slott solo: Big Time
sections.sub: 2010–13 · the arcs worth reading, issue by issue
sections.intro: Peter takes a job at Horizon Labs. Brighter, gadget-heavy, more optimistic.

items.note: “Big Time” begins — “Kill to be You”, Slott now writing alone, with Humberto Ramos
“Spider-Island” begins — all of Manhattan gets spider-powers
“Ends of the Earth” begins — Doc Ock
“Dying Wish” begins — the end of Slott's first era

sections.title: Superior Spider-Man
sections.sub: #1–33 · 2013–14 · if you read one thing after One More Day
sections.intro: The most contentious relaunch in the character's history — greeted with fury on announcement, and now widely considered the best Spider-Man run of the century. Thirty-three issues, finished, and it goes somewhere the main title never could.

items.note: “Spider-Verse” begins — the crossover the animated films drew from

sections.title: Amazing Spider-Man (2015–18)
sections.intro: Peter as globe-trotting CEO. Divisive, and the numbering changes partway when the title returns to its legacy count.

sections.title: Amazing Spider-Man (2018–22)
sections.intro: The best-regarded modern run on the main title, and it spends its full length building toward something.

sections.title: Amazing Spider-Man (2022–25)
sections.intro: The run that broke a lot of people's patience.

sections.title: Amazing Spider-Man (2025– )
sections.sub: #1–34 · Joe Kelly and Pepe Larraz · still running
sections.intro: Twice monthly and well received, building to ASM #1000 in September 2026. Marvel Unlimited adds issues about three months after print, so the last few are not readable there yet.

sections.title: Spider-Man: Life Story
sections.intro: Zdarsky and Bagley. One issue per decade, Peter ageing in real time from 1962. Self-contained, and arguably the finest Spider-Man comic of the last twenty years.

sections.title: Spider-Man: Blue
sections.intro: Loeb and Sale. A good decompression read after the classic run.
